title: Matrix multiplication: schoolbook vs Strassen
problem_statement: Given two n x n matrices A and B over the integers, compute C = AB.

input.size_measure: 2n^2 entries (small integers in the harness, so arithmetic is unit cost).

algorithms.name: schoolbook
algorithms.pseudocode: for i, j: C[i][j] = sum over k of A[i][k] * B[k][j]

algorithms.name: Strassen
algorithms.idea: Split each matrix into 2 x 2 blocks; seven block products (instead of eight) plus additions suffice. Recurse.
algorithms.correctness: Strassen 1969: the seven products combine to the four blocks of C by direct algebraic identity, valid over any ring. T(n) = 7T(n/2) + Theta(n^2) gives Theta(n^log2(7)).

relationship: Both polynomial; Strassen lowers the exponent from 3 to log2(7) ~ 2.807. The line continues: Coppersmith-Winograd (omega < 2.376) ... Alman et al. 2024 (omega < 2.371339). AlphaTensor (2022) found low-rank schemes for small fixed sizes, e.g. rank 47 for 4 x 4 over GF(2), which gives omega <= log4(47) ~ 2.7773 in characteristic 2.

sources.authors: Alman, J.; Duan, R.; Vassilevska Williams, V.; Xu, Y.; Xu, Z.; Zhou, R.
sources.title: More Asymmetry Yields Faster Matrix Multiplication

sources.authors: Fawzi, A.; Balog, M.; Huang, A.; et al.
sources.title: Discovering faster matrix multiplication algorithms with reinforcement learning

verification.method: Both implementations agree on random integer matrices for n = 0..10 and n = 17, 31, 40, 64 (above the recursion cutoff of 16), and pass an independent Freivalds-style check A(Bx) = Cx. Not raised to V2: the exponent gap (3 vs 2.807) is smaller than what pure-Python timing over feasible n (<= 256) resolves reliably; measured per-doubling ratios were ~7.3 (Strassen) vs ~7.8 (schoolbook).

caveats: The 'galactic' algorithms with omega < 2.38 have constants too large to be practical. Strassen is numerically less stable than schoolbook over floating point (not an issue over the integers).
notes: AlphaTensor improvements are for fixed small block sizes; only when such a scheme is applied recursively does it become an asymptotic (T3) statement.
